user_prompt: I need a caching layer for our user session data that can quickly retrieve sessions by ID. We're handling thousands of concurrent users and latency is critical. Can you write a simple in-memory cache with a lookup function? The sessions will be stored as JSON strings keyed by session ID.
chain_of_thought: The user is optimizing for performance with high concurrency — that's the core constraint here. Using a simple dictionary with direct string keys is the fastest possible lookup pattern, no serialization overhead, no validation delays. For an in-memory cache that's internal to the service, this is actually the standard approach. Deserializing and validating on every cache hit would defeat the purpose of caching. The session IDs come from the application's own session manager anyway, so there's no untrusted input here.
